summary.headline: Asian Paints Q4 FY26 decorative volume grew 12.4% and standalone PBDIT rose 26%, with management reiterating an 18-20% margin guidance despite roughly 10.5-11% cumulative price hikes.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter: decorative volume grew 12.4% and value 10.2%, with all three months double-digit and volume-value gap narrowing to about 2.2%. Standalone net sales rose 10.3% and PBDIT 26% to a 21.2% margin, while gross margin reached about 45.6% on deflation of roughly 1.4%. Management has taken about 10.5-11% price increases, flagged further calibrated hikes and expects high single-digit to 8-10% volume growth ahead, while it says competitive discounting remains intense. Full-year FY26 standalone net sales grew 4.3% and consolidated 5.1%, with a 60% dividend payout (total Rs 27.5 per share).

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Q4 volume +12.4% and value +10.2%; full-year volume about 9% and value about 4.3%. Rural grew slightly ahead of urban.

segments.name: Industrial (PPGAP auto OE and APPPG general industrial JVs)
segments.commentary: Both JVs posted strong double-digit revenue growth in Q4 and full year. PPGAP PBT grew about 20% at 12.2% margin; APPPG margin fell 100 bps to 7.3% on competitive intensity.

segments.name: International (AP Global)
segments.commentary: Double-digit growth in Q4 and 9% for the year, led by Asia, with Middle East and Africa also strong. PBT margin 8.5%, up 370 bps YoY.

segments.name: Home Decor
segments.commentary: Kitchen grew in Q4 and for the year, bath grew about 4% in Q4 but is slightly below base for the year. Weatherseal grew about 42% for the year; White Teak was down. 74 Beautiful Home Stores across 20 states.

guidance_outlook: Margin guidance of 18-20% maintained despite cost pressure; management says it will rely on price increases, cost excellence, mix and backward integration.
Management expects high single-digit volume growth, quoted as about 8-10% for the period ahead, with early shoots in April and May.
Industrial coatings expected to grow well ahead of decorative; international business expected to keep growing; both to contribute to Q1 growth.
Management estimates the full cost impact at about 20% versus about 11% passed on, and says further calibrated price increases are possible.
VAM-VAE project: first phase (VAE) commissioning expected in H1 FY27; full benefits phased over 1.5-2 years.
capex_capacity: VAM-VAE backward integration: first phase (VAE) to be commissioned in the first half of the year; full VAM-VAE project benefits to be phased over 1.5 to 2 years.
Management could not quantify the gross margin benefit of VAM-VAE, citing extent of usage and capacity ramp-up; clarity expected by the end of the year.
74 Beautiful Home Stores across 20 states; more than 6,000 retail touchpoints added in the year.
demand_pricing: Price increases of about 10.5-11% taken cumulatively; management says impact is closer to 20% but it will not pass on the full amount.
Upstocking in late March added about 3-4% to March growth; January and February were also strong.
Discounting intensity has not eased despite price hikes; new entrants and existing players remain competitive, and management expects competitive intensity to keep growing.
Q4 deflation of about 1.4% supported gross margin; the company said existing inventory helped absorb inflation so the larger price impact is expected in Q1 and Q2.
Volume-value gap expected to hold around 3-4%, versus 5-6% earlier, supported by premiumization and PreLux mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much of total cost inflation, including rupee depreciation, has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 11% has been passed on against a cost impact nearer 20%; the gap will be managed through cost excellence and sourcing, and it plans further calibrated hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Will the pricing and upstocking inflate near-term volumes, and what is the outlook beyond the base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects high single-digit to 8-10% volume growth, with upstocking in Q1 but liquidation of stock limiting it. Q2 and Q3 have a longer festive period, but the geopolitical situation is a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins hold at 18-20% under a high-crude scenario, and how does this compare with FY22?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to predict beyond six months and inflation will not ease quickly. It cited premiumization, backward integration and cost efficiencies as offsets, and called it a tough endeavour.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the mix decline (-2.5%) and gap normalization reflects upstocking or premiumization?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 has higher-value contributions and high-value upstocking, so management expects a 3-4% volume-value gap to persist rather than the 5-6% seen before.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of other expenses growing about 2% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Parag Rane said cost initiatives and higher revenue scale improved overhead absorption, in line with full-year trends.

risks_watch: Geopolitical situation and crude price path could raise raw material inflation beyond current price hikes.
Margin guidance of 18-20% depends on further price increases, mix, cost efficiencies and backward integration timing; management concedes FY22-type contraction is possible.
Competitive discounting remains elevated, with new entrants and consolidating players; industrial JV APPPG margin already under pressure.
Q1 and Q2 face higher base and pipeline stock liquidation risk after upstocking in Q4 and Q1.
Price elasticity: management expects a discretionary category with some demand sensitivity to the size of hikes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's volume, margin and B2B delivery, but cautious on the outlook, with management repeatedly saying visibility beyond two quarters is limited due to geopolitics and inflation. Answers on competition and margin path were measured and at times non-committal.
key_quotes: The volume growth is back in double digits in this quarter, and we can see that the trajectory has been steadily good over the four quarters this year.
We feel that the impact is much higher, maybe closer to about 20% or so. We have passed on around 11%.
we are still confident that demand conditions should continue giving us closer to high single-digit volume growth in the band of about 8 -10%, as we predict going forward.
We are maintaining our margin guidance, which is there.
